1507.01 OBJECT AND PURPOSE.
   The object and purpose of this Electrical Code is to safeguard persons and
property from hazards arising from the use of electrical energy by establishing
and adopting minimum standards for the installation and maintenance of
electrical systems, and further, to provide for the qualifying and licensing of
electrical contractors, the issuance of permits and collection of fees,
inspection and approval of material, equipment and installations and
administration and enforcement of the provisions and regulations contained
herein.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.015 NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE ADOPTED; COPIES.
   (a)    Under the provisions of Ohio R.C. 731.231, there is adopted by the
City, for the purpose of prescribing regulations governing conditions to
safeguard persons and property from the hazards arising from the use of
electrical energy, the National Electrical Code, recommended by the National
Fire Protection Association (NFPA #71-2002 Edition and all subsequent editions
thereafter) save and except such portions as may hereinafter be deleted,
modified or amended.
(Ord. 214-01. Passed 12-17-01.)
   (b)   A complete copy of such Code shall be kept on file at the office of
the Clerk of Council, the County Law Library and the City Electrician's office.
The Clerk of Council shall keep copies available for distribution to the public
at cost.
   (c)    For the purposes of the Codified Ordinances of the City, this section
will become a part of this chapter and from the date such National Electrical
Code shall take effect, the provisions thereof, except as are deleted, modified
or amended, shall be controlling within the City. (Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.02 SCOPE.
   This Electrical Code and the regulations included herein shall cover the
electrical conductors, apparatus and equipment and the installation, alteration
or repair of same for purposes of supplying and utilizing electricity for
light, heat, power, signal and controls, within or on public and private
buildings and other structures and premises within the City, including yards,
carnival lots, sales lots, parking lots, trailer or mobile home parks,
industrial substations, boat marinas, places of outdoor assembly and/or
recreation and electric signs and displays, also the conductors that connect
the installations to a supply of electricity, and other outside conductors on
or adjacent to the premises.
   This Electrical Code does not cover installations in mines, ships, railway
cars, automotive equipment or aircraft, or the installations and equipment
employed by a railway or an electric or communication utility in the exercise
of its function as a utility and located outdoors or in buildings used
exclusively for that purpose.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.03 ELECTRICAL REGISTRATION REQUIRED; HVAC CONTRACTORS.
   (a)   Except as otherwise provided herein for HVAC contractors, no person
shall install, maintain, alter or repair for others or engage in the business
of installing, maintaining, altering or repairing within the City any
electrical wiring, devices, apparatus or equipment unless such person shall
have received from the City, in accordance with the regulations herein, an
electrical contractor's registration and certificate for same, or unless he is
employed by and working under the direction of a holder of a Lorain City
electrical registration certificate.
   (b)   It shall be expressly recognized that HVAC contractors licensed by the
State of Ohio or the City of Lorain shall have the right to install any HVAC
wiring, devices, apparatus or equipment in single family residential units
located within the City. All such electrical work performed by any HVAC
contractor shall be inspected by an Electrical Inspector and approved only if
the work performed has been accomplished in a workmanlike manner in accordance
with all standards as are in existence or required to be followed at such time.
   (c)   HVAC contractors who undertake the installation of any HVAC wiring,
devices, apparatus or equipment in single family residential units located
within the City shall be required to demonstrate to the Chief Electrical
Inspector or the Chief Building Inspector upon request that such HVAC
contractor carries a general liability insurance policy with limits in an
amount which shall not be less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per
occurrence which policy shall be issued to protect the HVAC contractor's
customers or City residents in the event of any negligence attributable to such
HVAC contractor.
   (d)    The Service-Safety Director in conjunction with the Chief Electrical
Inspector and the Chief Building Inspector shall adopt rules which are to be
followed and adhered to by HVAC contractors and such rules shall be in keeping
with all State and Federal standards, laws, and regulations. Such rules shall
be properly communicated to all HVAC contractors upon renewal of their
registration certificates.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.04 REGISTRATION EXEMPTIONS.
   The electrical registration regulations of this chapfer shall not apply to
the following:
   (a)    The installation, alteration or repair of electrical generation,
transmission or distribution equipment, and utilization equipment owned and
operated by an electrical public utility company or the City.
   (b)   The installation, alteration or repair of signal or communication
equipment where such equipment is owned and operated by a public utility
company or the City.
   (c)    Any work in ships, railway cars, buses, aircraft, automobiles,
trailers and trailer houses.
   (d)    Any work in connection with electrical equipment used for radio and
television transmission, and including supply wires to such equipment.
   (e)   Any work involved in the manufacturing or testing of electrical
equipment or apparatus, but not including any permanent wiring or equipment.
   (f)   Any work associated with:
      (1)    The repair of plug-connected electrical appliances or devices;
      (2)    Permanently connected electrical appliances or devices which have
been electrically and mechanically disconnected and separated from all sources
of electrical supply by an electrical licensee. The opening of switches or the
blowing or removal of fuses shall not be considered as electricaI or mechanical
disconnection or separation.
   (g)    The installation or replacement of approved fuses which are not
oversize for the circuit involved.
   (h)    The installation or replacement of approved pin-type lamps, screw
base lamps or plug-connected portable appliances which do not overload the
circuit involved and are not located in hazardous locations.
   (i)    All work involved in the repairing and maintenance of elevators,
dumbwaiters and escalators.
   (j)   Homeowner's exception: permits will be required, but a registration
certificate will not be required for work covered in this Electrical Code
performed by the property owner himself upon his own single residence. This
exemption does not include others performing such work or the property owner
performing such work for others, nor does this exemption exempt any work from
any other requirements of this Electrical Code.
      (Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.05 BOND REQUIRED.
   Before receiving an electrical contractor's registration certificate, the
person, firm or corporation applying for same shall furnish a surety bond to
the City in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000), conditioned upon the
faithful performance by the registrant of all work entered into or contracted
for by said registrant, and upon the strict compliance by the registrant with
all provisions and requirements of the ordinances of the City relating to the
work performed under the registration certificate, and indemnifying the City
against all losses and damages by reason of any negligence on the part of the
registrant, or registrant's agents or employees, while engaged in the
prosecution of any business as such registrant. Bond shall be annually renewed.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.06 REGISTRATION APPLICATION.
   Applications for registration shall be made in writing to the Electrical
Inspection Department, stating the name, address and place of business of the
principal of the firm or corporation making the application and the name of the
representative of the applicant who will act as supervisor of work to be
performed under the registration certificate. All new applications for
registration shall possess a State of Ohio Electrical Contractor license.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.07 REGISTRATION HOLDER; DESIGNATED SUPERVISOR.
   Each applicant for a registration certificate issued in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter shall be known as the holder of the certificate and
he shall specify the name of the person who has passed the examination or who
will submit to examination, and such person shall be designated in the
certificate as the supervisor of all work to be performed under the
registration certificate. The designated supervisor may be the holder himself
if the holder is a person, or the supervisor may be an employee of or a member
of the firm, or if the holder is a corporation he may be an officer thereof.
The same person shall not be designated as the supervisor in two or more
certificates. If the business association with, or the employment of the
supervisor by the holder shall be terminated, then the registration certificate
shall become void after sixty days, unless another supervisor, qualified by
passage of the examination, shall he designated.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.08 REGISTRATION FEES AND TERM.
   Before a registration certificate as an electrical contractor is granted to
any applicant and before an expiring certificate is renewed, the applicant
shall pay the following registration fee to the City of Lorain, Division of
Buildings, Electrical Department as follows:
 
                          Initial Fee        Yearly
                          (New Registration) Renewal Fee
Any Electrical Contractor $175.00            $150.00
   Before the certificate may be issued or renewed the contractor shall
acknowledge to the Chief Building Inspector the contractor's obligation to
carry liability insurance both bodily injury liability and property damage
liability in an amount not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) for each
occurrence prior to beginning any work on any project in the City. All
electrical contractors and subcontractors who undertake work in the City shall
be required to demonstrate to the Chief Building Inspector at the time such
contractor seeks to pull a permit for any project or job, that such contractor
carries a general liability insurance policy with limits in an amount not less
than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence. Said policy shall be
issued to protect the public and the contractor's customers/citizens in the
event of any negligence attributable to such contractor. Upon the request of
any contractor's customer or upon the request of an electrical contractor in
privity of contract with a subcontractor, the contractor so requested shall
disclose and provide a copy of the insurance policy issued to him, her or it as
required in this section. Council expressly recognizes that this disclosure
requirement fosters consumer protection. Willfully working in the City as a
contractor without the required liability insurance shall be a cause for the
revocation of any contractor's license.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.09 PRIOR LICENSEES/REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES.
   Holders of a valid Lorain electrical contractor's license or registration
certificate on the date of the adoption of this Electrical Code (Ordinance
8839, passed September 21, 1964) or the effective date, whichever is later,
will be issued a renewal registration certificate upon payment of the renewal
fee when their present license or certificate expires, conditioned upon
compliance with all other stipulations of this Electrical Code.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.10 REGISTRATION RENEWAL.
   Each electrical contractor's license or registration certificate shall
expire as set forth in City of Lorain Codified Ordinance Section
1501.09(e) and shall be renewed by the Chief Electrical Inspector upon
application by the holder, upon the payment of the required renewal fee to the
City, and upon the submission of the renewal form for the surety bond as
required. Application for renewal must be made within thirty days of expiration
or the renewal fee will become the same as an original application.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.11 REGISTRATION REVOCATION; NONTRANSFERABLE.
   Any registered electrical contractor's registration may be suspended or
revoked by the Board of Building Standards and Appeal if the person holding the
registration certificate willfully, or by reason of incompetence, repeatedly
violates any statute of the State or any ordinance, rule or regulation of the
City relating to the installation, maintenance, alteration or repair of
electrical wiring, devices, appliances and equipment.
   No license and certificate issued m accordance with the provisions of this
Electrical Code shall be assignable or transferable.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.12 BOARD OF BUILDING STANDARDS AND APPEAL.
   The Board of Building Standards and Appeal policies, procedures and duties
are as established in City of Lorain, Codifed Ordinances Section
1501.10.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.13 AUTHORITY OF CHIEF INSPECTOR AND DEPUTIES.
   The Chief Electrical Inspector is hereby authorized to determine the intent
and meaning of all provisions and standards of this Electrical Code in the
first instance.
   He may delegate any of his powers or duties to his deputy inspector with
approval from the Service-Safety Director.
   Upon display of proper credentials, the Chief Inspector or his deputies
shall have the right to enter, at any reasonable time, any building, structure,
house, manhole or premises where construction, repair or remodeling is in
progress for the purpose of making inspections of electrical wiring or
equipment, and no person shall obstruct or interfere with the Chief Inspector
or his deputies in the discharge of their duties.
   The Chief Electrical Inspector, his assistants or any other personnel
connected with the Department of Electrical Inspection shall not have any
interest, financial or otherwise, in any electrical contracting or related
business.
   The Electrical Inspection Department shall not be permitted to design or lay
out installations or instruct untrained persons in the installation of
electrical systems or equipment.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.14 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall maintain, alter or repair any electrical wiring, devices,
appliances or equipment unless such person shall first obtain a permit from the
Electrical Inspection Department, or unless such person, or the work involved,
is specifically exempted by this Electrical Code. Work for which a permit has
been obtained must be commenced within six months or such permit shall become
null and void. A cessation of more than six months in work which has been
started will also void any permit.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.15 QUALIFICATION FOR OBTAINING PERMITS.
   Permits will be issued by the Electrical Inspection Department for all work
for which a permit is required to holders of valid electrical contractors
licenses upon payment of the required fees. But in no case shall any work
regulated herein be commenced until such permit has been issued.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.16 EXCEPTION.
   The owner of a single-family residence may obtain a permit for such
electrical work as may be required. Such owner of a single-family residence
will not be required to obtain a license but shall present in writing a signed
statement that all such work will be performed by himself; and such work shall
be subject to the approval of the Electrical Inspector.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.17 WORK OVER 32 VOLTS.
   All electric light or power work of any nature of thirty-two volts or over
is subject to City electrical permit.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.18 PERMIT APPLICATION.
   Application for permits shall be filed in writing with the Department of
Electrical Inspection on a form furnished for that purpose and signed by the
applicant. The application shall give the correct address of the work and
describe and enumerate the work, with such other information as may be required
.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.19 DRAWINGS REQUIRED.
   Drawings and specifications shall be required in sufficient detail to enable
the Department to determine that any proposed work for which a permit has been
applied for will be in conformity with the provisions of this Electrical Code.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.20 FEES.

1501.07.)
1507.21 APPROVAL OF MATERIAL.
   All electrical material, devices, fixtures, appliances, illuminated signs
and other equipment used or installed in the City shall be of a type approved
by the Board of Electrical Standards.
   Unless specifically disapproved by formal action of the Board of Electrical
Standards, electrical materials, devices, fixtures, appliances, illuminated
signs and other equipment that bear the label of approval of the Underwriters'
Laboratories, Inc., or other accredited agency, shall be deemed approved by the
Board.
   Old or secondhand material and equipment shall not be installed or used
unless approved as safe by the Electrical Inspection Department.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.22 INSPECTIONS, TESTS, APPROVALS.
   (a)    Authority of Inspection Department. All electrical wiring and
equipment installed, altered, replaced or repaired in or about any building,
structure or premises within the City shall be subject to inspection and
approval by the Electrical Inspection Department.
   (b)    Wiring to Be Left Open Until Inspection. No electrical wiring or
parts thereof shall be covered or concealed until the Electrical Inspection
Department has approved the installation and given permission to cover or
conceal same. It shall be the duty of the person obtaining the permit to give
twenty-four hours' notice to the Electrical Inspection Department when work is
ready for inspection. Work shall be inspected as soon as possible after receipt
of such notice, and, when found to conform to the provisions of this Electrical
Code, an official notice of approval shall be posted in a conspicuous place by
the inspector.
   (c)    Final Inspection; Certificate of Approval. All work covered by this
Electrical Code shall be submitted for final inspection and approval before
being placed in service. If the electrical wiring and equipment are found to be
complete and in conformity with all provisions of this Electrical Code, a
certificate of approval shall be issued by the Electrical Inspection
Department.
   (d)    Tests for Conformity. Tests necessary to verify that an installation
is in conformity with the requirements of this Electrical Code shall be
performed in the presence of an authorized inspector of the Electrical
Inspection Department, and any equipment, material, power and labor necessary
for such tests shall be furnished by the holder of the permit.
   (e)    Incompleteness or Nonconformity; Corrections; Stop Work Order. When
inspection shows work submitted for inspection is incomplete or not in
conformity with requirements of this Electrical Code, the permit holder shall
make the necessary corrections or additions within seventy-two hours and
resubmit the work for inspection. Failure to correct rejected work shall be
cause for issuance of a stop work order on the entire project.
   (f)    Reinspections. The Electrical Inspection Department may reinspect the
electrical wiring and equipment in all commercial buildings annually and in all
other buildings and structures at least once every three years, excepting one
and two-family dwellings which may be reinspected whenever vacated and before
being reoccupied by new owners or tenants.
   (g)    Time Limit for Repairs or Modifications. When wiring, devices and/or
apparatus are found, upon reinspection, to be defective or in any unsafe or
nonconforming condition, the necessary repairs or modifications shall be made
by the person owning, using or operating same, and such necessary repairs or
changes shall be made within ten days. Reasonable extensions of time may be
allowed by the Electrical Inspection Department when repairs or modifications
as required are begun within the ten-day period, but this work must be carried
to completion without undue delay.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.23 INSPECTION DEPARTMENT TO APPROVE ELECTRIC UTILITY CHANGES.
   (a)   The electric utility shall notify the Electrical Inspection Department
of all new meter applications or existent meter changes and shall not energize
or reenergize any wiring system without notification from the Electrical
Inspection Department that such wiring and apparatus conform, or have been
brought into conformity with the requirements of this Electrical Code.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
   (b)   There shall be a Meter Inspection fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) due
upon application for an electrical meter inspection for all requested
inspections.
(Ord. 63-21. Passed 4-19-21.)
1507.24 INSTALLATION STANDARDS.
   (a)    Conformity with Regulations. All installations of electrical wiring
and equipment for lighting, heating, signal or power shall be made in strict
accordance with the provisions of this Electrical Code and any orders, rules
and regulations issued by authority thereof. Where no specific standards are
prescribed by this Electrical Code or by any orders or statutes of the State,
the regulations of the Ohio Basic Building Code for safety of persons and
property shall be required under this Electrical Code. Conformity with the
regulations set forth by the latest National Electrical Code, as approved by
the American Standards Association, except as modified herein, shall be prima-
facie evidence of conformity with approved standards for safety of persons and
property.
   (b)   Wiring Methods. Wiring shall be installed in approved metallic raceway
in all institutional, commercial and industrial structures.
Exception No. 1. One, two and three family residences (see residential wiring
regulations, Section
1507.29.)
Exception No. 2. Underground installation, exclusive of installations made
under paving, buildings or other structures.
   (c)   Conductors for Earth Burial. Type USE and UF conductors may be used
for direct earth burial, in accordance with any current edition of the National
Electrical Code requirement, where not subject to mechanical injury. Where
considered necessary by the Electrical Inspection Department, supplementary
mechanical protection such as covering board, concrete pad and/or raceway may
be required.
   (d)    Conduits. Any conduit installed in concrete or below grade shall be
three-fourths inch minimum grade size galvanized rigid conduit.
   (e)    Wire Size for Over 50 Volts. Minimum wire size for all installations
carrying fifty volts or over shall be No. 12, except that No. 14 may be used
for general lighting circuits in one, two and three-family dwelling houses.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.25 RESIDENTIAL WIRING REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)    Nonmetallic sheathed cable may be used for the wiring of dwellings
and apartments arranged for one or more, but not more than twelve units.
   (b)    Residential buildings arranged for more than twelve dwelling units
shall be wired in approved metal raceway. The requirements for a main
disconnect shall be determined by a conforming fire wall, separating not more
than six dwelling units.
   (c)    In a multi-family dwelling, each individual apartment shall be
provided with not less than sixty-ampere main switch.
   (d)    All exposed wiring and outlets in basements shall be installed as per
the requirements of the current National Electrical Code.
   (e)    At least one outlet controlled by a wall switch shall be provided for
each habitable room, kitchen, toilet room, bathroom and garage. A lighting
outlet shall be provided at laundry trays, boilers, furnaces and other central
heating devices; three-way switches shall be provided for all stairways to
control lighting outlets illuminating such stairways. Hallways exceeding twelve
feet shall be controlled by three-way switches.
   (f)    In residences without basements and with a concrete floor slab,
wiring in slab shall be in rigid galvanized conduit, three-fourths inch
minimum, and wall switch outlets and plates and receptacle outlets and plates
shall be properly grounded unless constructed entirely of insulating material.
Note: Outlet boxes constructed of insulating material shall not be used with
metal raceway.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.26 SWIMMING POOL LIGHTING.
   See Article 680 of the National Electrical Code.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.27 SERVICE AND METERING.
   (a)    Service entrances on residential buildings must be installed in rigid
metal conduit not less than one and one-quarter inch I.D. and shall not be
concealed. The outside termination fitting or service head shall be of a type
designed for the purpose and shall in no case be less than twelve feet above
the ground or any platform.
   (b)   Meters or metering equipment inserted into the outside service conduit
shall be no higher than six feet above the ground or platform below the meter.
   (c)    Service entrance conductors shall not be less than No. 2 A.W.G.
copper.
   (d)    Service entrances shall be designed in accordance with load and
diversity requirements sufficient to carry the load according to the standards
of the National Electrical Code, current edition, but the minimum size for
individual residences shall be one hundred ampere three wire. Main
disconnecting means shall be required. If of the breaker type, breaker shall be
bolted down. One spare circuit shall be required for each five active circuits.
   (e)    Services supplying current at 600 volts or over shall not be attached
to buildings but shall be run underground, subject to approval of the
Electrical Inspection Department and electric utility company.
   (f)    Services and feeders supplying electrical heating loads shall be
calculated strictly in accordance with latest National Electrical Code
requirements and shall be installed in conformity with this Electrical Code by
licensed electrical contractors.
   (g)    The disconnecting means shall not be more than five feet six inches
or be less than two feet from the floor. Disconnecting means shall not be
placed in bed, bath or toilet rooms, in coal bins, elevators or ventilating
shafts, attics, stairways, show windows, or in pantries or clothes closets.
They shall not be placed over doorways, stoves, radiators, sinks, laundry tubs,
motors, wash stands or machinery. They shall not be placed closer than thirty-
six inches measured horizontally to stoves, radiators, sinks, laundry tubs,
motors, wash stands, gas meters or moving machinery, and shall not be placed on
insecure partitions or any wall subject to vibration.
   (h)    All circuits shall be marked or tagged in panels for lighting or
power, and location of circuits shall be marked on panel directory in
residential and commercial buildings.
   (i)    In apartments, duplex houses, etc., all meter switches shall be
plainly marked with metal tags showing to what set of rooms the wiring shall
belong. Installation of meter wiring and equipment shall generally conform to
requirements of the utility company as approved by the City Electrical
Inspector.
   (j)   Each service installation requires individual attention. Contractors
are requested to call the utility company for information on each installation
before proceeding with wiring. In such cases where the installation does not
meet the requirements of this Electrical Code, permission must be obtained from
the Electrical Inspection Department before installing the work.
   (k)   Every electrical contractor shall leave his name, address and
telephone number on the meter board to enable the Electrical Inspector to
communicate promptly with the contractor when necessary.
   (l)   Range cable shall be used on electric range installations and must
conform with the National Electrical Code.
   (m)    All circuits shall be protected by type “s” fuses or
noninterchangeable breakers.
   (n)    Recess fixtures shall be wired with type AF or AI fixture wire,
unless of a type especially approved for the purpose.
   (o)    All fluorescent lights on new installations and when replacing
ballasts on old installations must be protected by fuse mounted next to
ballast.
   (p)    Cleaning plants (as per National Electrical Code).
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.28 TEMPORARY SERVICES.
   The Electrical Inspection Department may grant special permission, for a
limited period of time, for the installation or use of temporary electric
service and wiring for emergencies or construction purposes, which may not
conform with the regulations of this Electrical Code. All such electric wiring
and equipment shall be isolated from the public by proper elevation, clearance
and guarding, and all overcurrent devices and disconnects shall be installed in
approved locations and enclosures.
   The person for whom such wiring is installed shall be directly and legally
responsible for maintaining the safe condition of the installation at all
times, and its complete removal at the end of the fixed temporary period, as
set by the Electrical Inspection Department, or any time sooner when ordered by
the Electrical Inspection Department.
   Carnivals, circuses, exhibitions and places of temporary outdoor assembly
are included in the provisions of this section, and all electric wiring and
equipment associated herewith shall be installed, maintained and operated in a
safe and workmanlike manner. Cable laid on the ground in areas traversed by the
public shall be buried or protected by approved covering.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.29 INSTALLATIONS USING OVER 600 VOLTS.
   Plans for installations of over 600 volts within buildings, including
transformers, switch gear, vaults and enclosures must meet the approval of the
Electrical Inspection Department, the Fire Chief and local utility company
before installation is begun.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.30 HAZARDOUS LOCATIONS.
   Gasoline dispensing stations and other installations defined by the National
Electrical Code as Class 1 - Division 1 Hazardous Location, where volatile,
flammable liquids or gases are utilized, stored or dispensed, shall be wired
strictly in accordance with all current National Electrical Code requirements.
Gasoline dispensing pumps shall not be connected more than two to a circuit.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.31 EMERGENCY LIGHTING.
   Article 700 of the National Electrical Code, latest issue, shall be
enforced.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.32 EXTERIOR WIRING.
   All corporations, copartnerships, associations or individuals, or agents
thereof operating in the City, must install and maintain all their exterior and
service wires in any street or alley in the manner required by the Regulations
of the Ohio Public Utilities Commission or any orders or regulations now or
hereafter existing, made by any duly authorized authority pursuant to the
provisions of the Regulations of the Ohio Public Utilities Commission.
   All poles or wires which are not in use and are not maintained in accordance
with the safety provisions of this Electrical Code shall, upon written notice
by the Chief Electrician, be repaired or removed by the corporation,
copartnership, association or individual who owns, operates, controls, manages
or has charge of such wires and poles.
   All City signal or light wires removed for any cause shall be replaced by
parties removing same to the satisfaction of the Chief Electrician and at no
expense to the City.
   The Chief Electrician shall have the power to require all exterior and
service wires to be placed and maintained as provided for in this Electrical
Code, and on written notice from the Chief Electrician to any corporation,
copartnership, association or individual, or agent thereof, calling for the
correction or removal of any wires or poles or electrical apparatus of any
kind, maintained contrary to the provisions of this Electrical Code, the same
shall be immediately removed or corrected by such corporation, copartnership,
association or individual, or agent thereof, controlling, managing or owning
such wires, poles or apparatus. The Chief Electrician is also authorized and
empowered to cause the turning off of the electric current from all conductors
or apparatus which is deemed by him to be unsafe or which has not been
installed in conformity with the provisions of this Electrical Code.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.33 IN CASE OF FIRE.
   The Fire Chief or the Chief Electrician or some other competent person
delegated by them, or either of them, to do so, shall have the power to at once
cause the removal of all wires or the turning off of all electrical currents,
or both, where the circuit interferes with the work of the Fire Department
during the progress of a fire.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.34 NEW HOMES AND OLDER HOMES.
   (a)    Grounding. All outlets shall be grounded and U-shaped grounded
receptacles throughout (three-wire grounded type).
   (b)   Box Fill. Box fill shall be according to paragraph 370-6, National
Electrical Code.
   (c)    Kitchen.
      (1)   The following shell be circuited separately:
         Dishwasher.
      (2)    Remaining receptacles shall be wired in the following manner:
         Two outlets first circuit;
         Three outlets thereafter.
         No. 12 wire for receptacles.
An appliance outlet shall be installed for the refrigerator, one on either side
of kitchen sink and at other locations in the work area or so laid out to equal
every twelve feet of the entire room.
   
   (d)    Dining Room. Receptacles shall be wired with No. 12 wire every twelve
feet. This room may be wired in with the kitchen circuits.
   (e)   Living Room. A receptacle every twelve feet and no more than six
outlets per circuit and No. 14 gauge wire permissible.
   (f)   Bedrooms and Bathroom. A receptacle every twelve feet and no more than
eight outlets per circuit and No. 14 wire. Bathroom may be included with
bedroom circuiting.
   (g)    Basements. All basements shall be wired in conduit or E.M.T. with
conduit fill as per National Electrical Code.
      Circuit #1 - Furnace (with fusestat) No. 14 wire.
      Circuit #2 - Washing machine, grounded type receptacle No. 12 wire.
      Circuit #3 - Gas dryer, grounded type receptacle No. 12 wire.
      Circuit #4 - Sump pump, grounded type receptacle No. 14 wire.
   (h)   Special Equipment. Any air conditioner, electric heater or other
special equipment shall be wired on a separate circuit.
   (i)    Utility Room. Separate circuit for furnace. Washing machine and, if
gas dryer, a separate circuit No. 12 gauge wire.
   (j)    Garage. At least one base plug shall be installed. One light a
minimum with switch.
   (k)   Doors Leading to Outside. All doors leading to the outside shall be
illuminated by a light on the outside controlled by a wall switch located just
inside such doorway.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.35 POSITIONS DEFINED.
   The term “Chief Electrician” shall be synonymous with the term “Chief
Electrical Inspector” as they are used in this Electrical Code and falling
within the purview of this designation shall be the position of the
Superintendent of the Police and Fire Alarm Telegraph of the City.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.36 LIABILITY.
   This Electrical Code shall not be construed as imposing on the City any
liability or responsibility for damages resulting from any defective electrical
work or equipment, or installation thereof, nor shall the City or any official
or employee thereof be held as assuming any liability or responsibility by
reason of any act or action taken in enforcing the provisions of this
Electrical Code or carrying out the duties authorized and required by this
Electrical Code. Any lawsuit or action brought against any City official,
employee or board member by reason of any act or action committed in the
discharge of their duties under this Electrical Code shall be defended by the
City Solicitor until final termination of proceedings in such action.
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1507.99 PENALTY.
   Every corporation, copartnership, association or individual, and every
servant or agent of any corporation, copartnership, association or individual,
who shall violate or disregard any provisions or requirements of this
Electrical Code shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction
thereof, shall be fined not less than five dollars ($5.00) and not more than
two
hundred dollars ($200.00)
(Ord. 2-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
CHAPTER 1509
Property Maintenance Code
1509.01   Adoption.
1509.02   Provisions additional, not superseding.
1509.03   Adoption not affecting existing ordinances.
1509.04   Amendments.
1509.05   Temporary protection.
1509.06   Notices and orders.
1509.07   Form.
1509.08   Method of service.
1509.09   Unauthorized tampering.
1509.10   Definitions.
1509.99   Failure to comply with a notice or neglect of maintenance.
 
CROSS REFERENCES
Adoption by reference - see Ohio R.C. 731.231
Housing Board of Appeals - see BLDG. Ch.
1521
 
1509.01 ADOPTION.
   The City of Lorain does hereby adopt as and for its Property Maintenance
Code certain documents as attached as Exhibit "A" to original Ordinance 106-09,
passed August 26, 2009, and designated as the Lorain Property Maintenance Code,
Chapters One through Nine. Such Property Maintenance Code and all subsequent
editions of same are hereby adopted by reference herein as if fully rewritten
and are made a part of the Codified Ordinances as new Chapter
1509. Such Property Maintenance Code is adopted from the International Property
Maintenance Code, as has been published by the International Code Council.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.02 PROVISIONS ADDITIONAL, NOT SUPERSEDING.
   The Property Maintenance Code provisions are an additional chapter of the
Codified Ordinances and do not replace or modify standards otherwise
established for construction, replacement or repair of buildings. Where a
provision of this chapter is found to be in conflict with any provision in any
building, zoning, housing or health department ordinance or regulation, or any
other ordinance or statute of this State or the United States of America, then
the provisions which establish the higher standard for the protection of
health, safety, and welfare shall prevail, and nothing in this chapter shall be
construed to supersede, limit, modify or replace any other powers or duties of
the Board of Health, Fire Chief or Electrical Inspector of the City.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.03 ADOPTION NOT AFFECTING EXISTING ORDINANCES.
   Nothing in this chapter or in the Property Maintenance Code hereby adopted
shall be construed so as to affect any suit pending in any court, or any
enforcement of any existing ordinance or portion thereof nor shall any legal
right or remedy be lost or affected by this chapter.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.04 AMENDMENTS.
   EDITOR'S NOTE: At the time of the publication of the 2007 update to the
Lorain Codified Ordinances the City was in the process of establishing
amendments to the Property Maintenance Code. See the Clerk of Council for the
current status of such amendments.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.05 TEMPORARY PROTECTION.
   No person shall use a tarp, black plastic, or similar material in place of a
customary building component for siding, doors, windows, roofs, or similar
components, for a period exceeding ninety (90) days in total, whether such use
is continuous or interrupted, except when a longer period is needed for the
processing of an insurance claim or the Code Enforcement Officer grants a one-
time extension for up to thirty (30) days.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.06 NOTICES AND ORDERS.
   Whenever the Chief Building Official or his/her designee determines that
there has been a violation of this code or has grounds to believe that a
violation has occurred, notice shall be provided in the manner prescribed in
Section
1509.07 and
1509.08 to the property owner, person in possession of the property or both for
the violation as specified in this code.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.07 FORM.
   Such notice prescribed in Section
1509.06 shall be in accordance with all of the following:
   (a)   Be in writing;
   (b)   Include a description of the real estate sufficient for
identification;
   (c)   Include a statement of the violation or violations and why the notice
is being issued;
   (d)   Include a correction order allowing a reasonable time to make repairs
or improvements, as determined by the Chief Building Official, required to
bring the dwelling unit or structure into compliance with the provisions of
this code;
   (e)   Inform the property owner of the right to appeal; and
   (f)   Include a statement of the right to file a record against the property
for not being brought into compliance with the property maintenance code.
      (Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.08 METHOD OF SERVICE.
   Such notice shall be deemed to be properly served if a copy thereof is:
   (a)   Delivered personally;
   (b)   Sent by certified or first-class mail to the last known address of the
property owner;
   (c)   If the notice is returned showing that the letter was not delivered, a
copy thereof shall be posted in a conspicuous place in or about the structure
affected by such notice; or
   (d)   Posted in a newspaper of general circulation.
      (Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.09 UNAUTHORIZED TAMPERING.
   Signs, tags or seals posted or affixed by the code official shall not be
tampered with, defaced, mutilated, destroyed or removed without authorization
of the code official.
(Ord. 72-16. Passed 7-18-16.)
1509.10  DEFINITIONS.
   For the purposes of this Code, the following words and phrases shall have
the meaning set forth as follows:
   (a)    "Dwelling" means a building providing complete, independent living
facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living,
sleeping, cooking, earing and sanitation.
   (b)    "Family" means an individual or two or more persons living together
as a single housekeeping group in a dwelling.
   (c)    "Housing License" means application form provided by the Building
Department that authorizes the operation of a rental dwelling.
   (d)    "Non-resident" means the owner of a rental dwelling, who at the time
of application for a housing license does not reside within Lorain County and/
or adjoining counties, i.e. Cuyahoga, Erie, Huron, Ashland, Medina or relocates
outside these counties after they have been issued a housing license for a
rental dwelling.
   (e)    "Occupant" means a family or family member living in a rental
dwelling.
   (f)    "Owner" means any legal person, the owner or owners of the premises,
including the holder of title thereto subject to contract of purchase, a vendee
in possession, a mortgagee or receiver in possession, a lessee or joint lessees
of the whole thereof or an agent or any other person, firm or corporation
directly in control of the premises. (Ord. 216-23. Passed 10-16-23.)
1509.99 FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH A NOTICE OR NEGLECT OF MAINTENANCE.
   (a)    A person who or which refuses, neglects or fails to comply with an
order issued under the provisions of this Code or other applicable Codes of the
City of Lorain; or refuses, neglects or fails to comply with a notice to
repair, rehabilitate or demolish a building or other structure declared to be
unsafe under the provisions of this Code, or refuses, neglects or fails to
comply with a notice requiring the abatement or removal of a violation or
requiring a compliance with any provisions of this Code or other applicable
Codes or any rule or regulation hereunder within the time limit set forth in
such notice or maintains a use or occupancy prohibited by this Code, shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree.
   (b)    The imposition of any penalty shall not preclude the Director of Law
from instituting an appropriate action or proceeding in a court of proper
jurisdiction to prevent an unlawful repair or maintenance or to restrain,
correct or abate a violation or to prevent the occupancy of a building,
structure or premises, or to require compliance with the provisions of this
Code, or other applicable laws, ordinances, rules or regulations, or the orders
or determinations of the Building Commissioner, the Mayor, the Board of Zoning
Appeals and Board of Building Standards and Building Appeals.
(Ord. 216-23. Passed 10-16-23.)
CHAPTER 1511
Plumbing Code
1511.01   Contractor registration.
1511.02   Registration application.

1511.09   Plans and work description.

Plumbing - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3703
 
1511.01 CONTRACTOR REGISTRATION.
   No person or persons, firm, company or corporation shall engage in or work
at the trade or occupation of plumbing contractor in the City of Lorain until
such person, persons, firm, company or corporation has been duly registered,
bonded and insured in accordance with City of Lorain Codified Ordinance Section
1501.09.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.02 REGISTRATION APPLICATION.
   Applications for registration shall be in writing stating the name, address
and place of business of the principal of the firm, company or corporation
making the application. All new applications for registration shall possess a
State of Ohio Plumbing Contractor’s License. Upon approval, registration shall
be in accordance with City of Lorain Codified Ordinance Section
1501.09(e) and (f). Renewal of existing registration, upon expiration, will
also be in accordance with Section
1501.09 of the City of Lorain Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.03 BOARD OF BUILDING STANDARDS AND APPEALS.
   The Board of Building Standards and Appeals policies, procedures and duties
are as established in City of Lorain Codified Ordinance Section
1501.10.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.04 CHIEF PLUMBING INSPECTOR DUTIES.
   The Chief Plumbing Inspector shall hold a State of Ohio, Department of
Commerce certification as a Certified Plumbing Inspector and maintain said
certification in good standing. The Chief Plumbing Inspector shall take
direction from the Chief Building Official, review plans, be versed in and have
knowledge of all plumbing codes and any applicable codes. The Chief Plumbing
Inspector shall maintain mandatory continuing education requirements.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.05 REGISTRATION SUSPENSION AND/OR REVOCATION.
   All suspension and/or revocation hearings shall be in accordance with the
Board of Building Standards and Appeals procedures as set forth in Sections
1501.09(g) and (h) and Section
1501.10(a) through (e).
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.06 PLUMBING PERMIT ISSUANCE AND USE OF NAME.
   Plumbing permits shall only be issued to a duly licensed plumbing contractor
registered with the City of Lorain (except for homeowners performing work in
their own homes). The plumbing contractor shall not permit his/her license to
be used by any other person, persons, firm, company or corporation not duly
licensed/registered under such license. Should the duly licensed/registered
person leave the employment of the person, persons, firm, company or
corporation registered with the City of Lorain as a plumbing contractor or
business, that person, persons, firm, company or corporation shall no longer
engage in plumbing work in the City of Lorain.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.07 TRANSFERRING PLUMBING PERMIT.
   No plumbing permit issued to a duly licensed plumbing contractor may be used
by another licensed plumber, either to start or complete an existing job,
without first submitting a letter from the original plumbing contractor to the
Plumbing Inspector releasing himself from the permit and responsibility for the
job the permit was issued for without any refund of permit fees. The new
plumbing contractor may then re-apply for a permit. He must pay the full permit
fee, and assume full responsibility for the entire plumbing system whether the
job has started or is new.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.08 PERMITS REQUIRED AND FEES.
   (a)   No plumbing work shall be performed in the City of Lorain except in
the case of repairs, leaks or maintenance without a permit being first
obtained. Applications for permits shall be made on forms provided by the City
of Lorain, Division of Buildings.
   (b)   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Former subsection (b) was repealed by Ordinance 40-04,
passed April 5, 2004. For permit fees, see Section
1501.07.)
   (c)   Beginning work without a permit shall result in payment of double the
original fee.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.09 PLANS AND WORK DESCRIPTION.
   No plumbing permits shall be issued until suitable plans and a description
in triplicate of the work to be done have been submitted and approved.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.10 WORK TO BEGIN IN SIX MONTHS.
   If the work is not begun under the approved plans within six months from the
date of approval, the permit shall be deemed to have expired.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.11 RECORD OF PLANS AND BUILDING PLUMBING.
   The Chief Plumbing Inspector shall keep a record of all plans and
descriptions submitted to him hereunder, together with his action thereon, and
he shall also make a record of the plumbing in each building in the City of
Lorain.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.12 OHIO PLUMBING CODE APPLICATION.
   The Ohio Plumbing Code, 1998 Edition, shall apply to all plumbing, sewer and
general sanitation in all structures and buildings in the City of Lorain.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.13 INSPECTOR’S CONFLICT OF INTEREST.
   Plumbing inspectors shall not, during their term of office, be engaged or
interested in the plumbing business or the sale of any plumbing supplies, nor
shall they act as agent, directly or indirectly, for any person or persons so
engaged.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.14 VIOLATION CEASES WORK.
   In the case of the violation of the foregoing rules and regulations or any
part thereof, the approval of the plans and the permit shall be nullified by
the Division of Buildings and written notice shall at once be given to the
plumbers having charge of the work and doing the same, and the owner of the
building or his agent, and thereupon shall not recommence until such plans and
permit have been reapproved.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
1511.15 DISPOSITION OF FEES.
   All moneys and fees collected under the provisions of this chapter shall be
deposited into the General Fund of the City.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
   
1511.99 PENALTY.
   Any person, firm or corporation which fails to comply with any of the
provisions of this chapter or with any of the requirements hereof or any
regulations hereunder shall be guilty of a first degree misdemeanor.
(Ord. 5-01. Passed 1-16-01.)
CHAPTER 1513
Grading Regulations
1513.01   Certified grading/certificate of occupancy.
